scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8129: HELP!! PC11 (the VLAN 20 workstation, 172.16.20.x) has
completely FALLEN OFF the network. It can't reach its gateway, can't reach
its neighbours, can't reach ANYTHING -- a total brick. Its port on the switch
has obviously been shut off -- the machine is fine, its socket into the
network is dead, I'd put money on it!! It worked on Friday! Please turn
PC11's switch port back on (or move it to a working one) and put it back on
the network!! Work is piling up on that desk!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC11 (172.16.20.x on VLAN 20) reaches its
  gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0% loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and
  reaches off-subnet destinations across the core (OSPF converged). The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a single-host
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC11 isolated from
everything -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0%
loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and reaches off-subnet hosts (e.g. a
Campus 2 or other-VLAN address) across the converged core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: PC11's connectivity is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces PC11's gateway,
intra-VLAN, and inter-subnet reachability, finds them working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a disabled port or an isolated host -- blaming the
switch port, the VLAN 20 SVI, or PC11's config to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk ticket claims PC11 (172.16.20.11) is completely unreachable and
that its switch port has been administratively shut down. Direct live
inspection of every element in the data path finds no fault whatsoever.

PC11's eth0 interface is UP with the correct address (172.16.20.11/24) and
the correct default gateway (172.16.20.254). Its access port — switch2.eth5,
connected via the access_vlan20_port6 collision domain — is UP, a member of
the br_vlan20 Linux bridge, and in the "forwarding" STP state. There is no
administrative shutdown anywhere in the path. PC11's MAC address
(7a:50:0d:db:6a:15) is actively learned in switch2's bridge forwarding
database on eth5, confirming bidirectional L2 reachability.

Layer-3 tests confirm full end-to-end connectivity: PC11 reaches its gateway
(mswitch0 vlan20 SVI, 172.16.20.254) with 0% packet loss, reaches the VLAN
10 SVI (172.16.10.254) via inter-VLAN routing, reaches its VLAN 20 peers
PC9 (172.16.20.9) and PC10 (172.16.20.10), and reaches WAN-side router
addresses (192.168.10.1, 172.30.1.1). Reverse-path tests from PC9 back to
PC11 also succeed. mswitch0 holds a complete OSPF routing table with routes
to all known subnets.

Root cause: there is no fault. The ticket premise is incorrect — PC11's port
has never been shut, and the workstation has full network connectivity.

Corrective action: none required on the network side. The reporter should
re-test from the workstation directly; the outage they experienced was either
transient (e.g., a momentarily unresolved ARP cache at first boot) or was
caused by a host-side application issue unrelated to the network.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly verifies PC11 reaches its gateway (172.16.20.254), same-VLAN peers, and off-subnet destinations with 0% packet loss, matching the baseline-healthy requirement.

The agent ran appropriate L2/L3 checks (interface states, bridge FDB, ARP/arping, and multiple pings including gateway, VLAN peers, cross-VLAN and WAN) and concluded there is no network fault; most claims are backed by the log outputs though a minor MAC/port naming inconsistency is present. Overall the evidence supports the negative-control conclusion that PC11 is healthy.
